passages.quote: flip, direction, answer hidden in the starting points, where the jobs came from, add a job, look inside, pairs that pull, catch-alls and their gauges, what the change list leaves out, rivals, and where the parts came from.
passages.reading_a: The eleven tests in other words: "direction" is Step 5's Reverse test (poke the supposed cause and see if the effect moves; poke the effect and see that the cause does not), and "catch-alls and their gauges" is Check the patches entire (what was rescued before, plus a gauge for any catch-all).
passages.reading_b: "Direction" is a verdict on which way the argument runs - the forward/backward kinds named in Step 1 - and "catch-alls and their gauges" is only the catch-all half. Reverse and the patch history then have no slot in the template and are not run.
passages.resembles: H64 kind 2: "the seven-heading report in SKILL.md gives no heading for the jobs list Step 2 requires, and its whole-explanation-checks line ... names no slot for *look inside* or *add a job*; 'a reader filling this template exactly, as this one did, has no slot' for them." Change 2 cut slots for those two tests and left these two renamed.
passages.would_break: A section headed "Direction" that reads "Most of the paper runs forward from assumptions to equations" and nothing about poking either end, with no two-sided poke anywhere in the report; and a "Catch-alls" section with no question about what was rescued when the explanation was caught out before. Taken in the record: of the 195 replies in rigs/plan 49 rig .../runs, runs_repeat, runs_repeat_31, runs_sonnet5, runs_sonnet5_31, 103 carry a "Direction" section and 96 of those contain no "poke the cause/effect", "change the cause/effect", "step in and change" or "intervene on" anywhere in the reply (some discuss direction of causation in other words; what is missing is the two-sided poke the Reverse bullet asks for); 70 of the 133 replies that name a catch-all carry no patch-history word at all. A marker under plan 52 would NOT call it the skill's fault: file 54 marked reverse RAN in "12 to 15" of 16 and check-the-patches RAN "in every skill-mode report", so the substitution passed as the test run, and H64's second marker put reverse at 40 of 48 and patches at 41. The break is invisible to the marking rather than absent from the reports.
passages.single_reading_wording: flip, reverse (poke the cause, then poke the effect), answer hidden in the starting points, where the jobs came from, add a job, look inside, pairs that pull, check the patches (what was rescued before, and a gauge for every catch-all), what the change list leaves out, rivals, and where the parts came from.

passages.quote: For each part, name one change to the world that should alter the outcome, and one that should not. A part with no such pair is a label, not a working part.
passages.reading_a: The two changes must sit close enough together that a label could fail: the "would not" change tests the nearby disputed boundary.
passages.reading_b: Any pair satisfies it. A change that plainly could not matter can be found for any part whatever, so every part passes and nothing is ever called a label.
passages.resembles: None recorded as a break in 54, H57, H62 or H64. H64's trap line points at it from outside: "The disagreements sit on four tests (poke, add a job, swap, inside), and those are where the skill's wording is loosest by the second marker's own breaks" (poke agreed 35 of 48, the lowest of the eleven). The other project records the same device failing outright: "The judgement-phrase pass written into file 30 could be passed by any phrase at all: it asked for one change showing "met" and one showing "unmet", and far-apart changes are always available. Shown on first use: zero marks in 32 rows" (Language/records/Checked reasoning language - Lessons.md, entry 35, checked verbatim).
passages.would_break: Poke pairs whose second half is chosen far from the boundary - "Poke: prove P=NP and the conclusion (Hilbert's dream revives) flips; write the proofs out longer and it does not" (runs/C2-m2) - so the pair is always available and the trap "Mistaking a label for a part" never fires: my search of the 195 replies found a part called a label in six of them. A marker under plan 52 would not call it the skill's fault; the mark is RAN, "applied with a concrete change", and file 54 duly records poke RAN in 11 to 12 of 16. The line that would close it has been held out of the skill since log 42 and the criterion of closeness exists, written by an outside author: "the original unmet change removes the relevant ability, route or grounds wholesale, or jumps to an unsupported extreme, rather than testing the nearby disputed boundary" (Semantics/results/S62 .../05 Near-case coverage of the table.md, checked verbatim).
passages.single_reading_wording: For each part, name one change to the world that should alter the outcome, and one that should not - and the second must sit next to the disputed boundary, not remove the ability, route or grounds wholesale. A pair that could be found for any part at all is not a pair.

passages.quote: fixed (a job or requirement the owner put outside the test, and said so; not a part the owner merely asserts, which is inside the test, has the provenance *asserted*, and takes whatever mark holds it; and not a free choice, which is loose)
passages.reading_a: The mark says: this part is itself the thing the owner put outside the test, and said so.
passages.reading_b: The mark says: this part is held by a job or requirement the owner put outside the test - so any part doing a job tagged fixed is marked fixed. The definition names "a job or requirement", and a part is neither.
passages.resembles: H57 break 2: "'| P7 [this lever sends it into the future, this one reverses] | fixed | the owner set it...' ... The reader has read 'the owner' as the author of the document, which the framing text invites, and has then used *fixed* for any untested assertion of his. That is the skill's wording permitting the error, in a second way." Also H62's "*fixed* put on the derivation itself".
passages.would_break: A mark cell reading "fixed - the owner set it" on a free design choice or on an author's say-so; the part is then reported as outside the test and never marked by what holds it. Yes, a marker under plan 52 calls this the skill's fault and has done so twice: file 54's break 2 and H57's recurrence were both recorded as the skill's, and H64's blind second marker flagged the same table row unprompted ("quoting the same table row ('P7 | fixed | the owner set it')"). Change 1 does not close this reading: it forbids *fixed* as a provenance, and this reading keeps *fixed* in the mark column, where the break happened.
passages.single_reading_wording: fixed (this part is one the owner put outside the test, and said so; a part that merely does a job tagged fixed takes whatever mark holds it, as does a part the owner merely asserts; a free choice is loose)

passages.quote: - **Where each part came from.** Built (a test here forced it), borrowed (rests on another explanation; name it, and name its best rival), or fitted.
passages.reading_a: The places a part can come from are four (built, borrowed, fitted, and asserted from Step 6), so *borrowed* is a provenance and the new paragraph's ban governs only the judging path.
passages.reading_b: The new paragraph is the skill's rule everywhere ("*borrowed* and *fixed* are not provenances"), so this bullet is wrong: a part that rests on another explanation must be given one of fitted, built or asserted, and *borrowed* belongs in the mark column only.
passages.resembles: H64 kind 1: "the eight part-marks (held, held if, ..., borrowed, fixed, unknown) and the provenance words (fitted, built, asserted) are two closed lists in the same style, and 'nothing in the skill says the two vocabularies must not be mixed'; readers put *asserted* in the mark column and *borrowed* or *fixed* in the provenance column."
passages.would_break: A provenance line reading "*Provenance:* most parts are **borrowed** from Jacobson (refs [2],[3]) and the BSD implementation" (runs/D2-m2) or "**Provenance:** P1 asserted/borrowed" (runs_sonnet5_31/P3-m1-r1): three of the 195 replies write borrowed as a provenance, exactly the half of the collision H64 named, and file 32 now forbids it in SKILL.md while its own building module still teaches it and the word list gives only three provenance rows (fitted/built/asserted). A marker under plan 52 can record this as the skill's fault only if it opens building.md; the quoted line it would have to cite is in a module the router opens only for things that do not exist yet, and H67's frozen recurrence line covers the mirror case (a provenance word in the mark column) and not this one.
passages.single_reading_wording: - **Where each part came from.** Built (a test here forced it), fitted, or asserted. A part that rests on another explanation is *marked* borrowed - name that explanation and its best rival; that is a mark, not a provenance.

passages.quote: held if (held only by a job, or only by another part, that is itself in doubt; name it)
passages.reading_a: "In doubt" means the other part carries a mark that is not held: loose, idle or unknown.
passages.reading_b: "In doubt" means the other part is untested or unproved here, whatever mark it carries.
passages.resembles: H64 kind 3: "the mark is defined only by a doubtful job, so a part that rests on another part, or two parts jointly necessary and neither sufficient, gets a hybrid mark the list does not contain ('Held - only as a pair with C')." This clause is the fix written for it.
passages.would_break: Both readings are already in the record under the older wording, with different grounds. Reading A: "P6 | held if | Held only by P5 and P7, both loose." (runs_repeat_31/F4-m1-r3). Reading B: "5.2 export controls secondary | **Held if** - held only by the asserted claim that all required technology can be made in every country. That claim is not tested here" (runs/D1-m1) - and "not tested here" is the skill's definition of *borrowed* ("held in place by some other explanation that is not being tested here"), so under reading B two of the eight marks fit the same part and the choice is the reader's. A marker under plan 52 has no rule to prefer either, so this would come out as marker disagreement, not as the skill's fault - the outcome H64 already reported for three fields it then struck ("the criterion's words are read two ways and the field says nothing until they are fixed").
passages.single_reading_wording: held if (held only by a job you added, or only by a part that is itself marked loose, idle or unknown; name it, and what would settle it. A part held by something outside this explanation is *borrowed*, not *held if*)

passages.quote: A part that two others hold only together is *held, jointly with* the other, named.
passages.reading_a: A part held only by two other parts acting together: name both of them.
passages.reading_b: Two parts that do one job only together: each is *held, jointly with* the one other, named - which is what SKILL.md says ("where two parts hold a job only together, say \"held, jointly with\" and name the other").
passages.resembles: H64 kind 3, quoted above, whose own case is the row the second marker quoted: "**Held - only as a pair with C** | ... Cut B alone and J2 survives on C; cut B and C together and J2 goes unanswered. A group, not two routes." (marking/to_mark.md, report 043/048).
passages.would_break: Under reading A a mark cell reads "held, jointly with B and C"; under reading B two cells each read "held, jointly with the other" - a different report of the same finding, from the two sentences that introduce the same new phrase ("two others ... the other" against "two parts ... the other"). The report's own item 3 was not changed and still says only "held (by which job or change)", so a reader filling the template never meets the phrase. The motivating case itself reads two ways: the reader wrote "Cut B alone and J2 survives on C", which is the skill's definition of *two routes* ("either of two parts does the job"), while the second marker described it as "neither B alone nor C alone but only both together" - so the clause may not fit the case that forced it. A marker under plan 52 would not call the new phrase a break, since the skill instructs it; a marker under H67's frozen line ("any word not one of the eight, as a mark") would flag "held, jointly with C" as a non-eight mark.
passages.single_reading_wording: Where two parts do a job only together and neither does it alone, mark each *held, jointly with* the other, named - and put the same words in the report's item 3.

passages.quote: The eight marks (Step 3's list) say what holds a part in place now; the provenance words (fitted, built, asserted) say where it came from.
passages.reading_a: The list in the report's item 3, which does hold the eight marks.
passages.reading_b: The list made at Step 3 of the procedure - "List the parts that are claimed to do the work" - which is a list of parts and holds no marks at all. The paragraph sits among the numbered Steps, so this is the nearer referent of "Step 3".
passages.resembles: H64 kind 1, quoted above: this paragraph is the change written to close it, and its pointer to the closed list is wrong.
passages.would_break: A reader who follows the pointer finds the parts list and no eight words against which to check the mark column; the closed list is in "How to ask" (a section about questioning a person), in the report's item 3, in reporting.md's table and in question-bank section 7. The risk is the very fault the paragraph exists to stop - a word that is not one of the eight in the mark column - and twelve mark cells in the 195 replies already are one (built 5, asserted 4, fitted 3), with hybrids like "**Held** (vacuity point) / **Asserted** (waterfall conjecture)" (runs/C2-m2). No run can show which reading a reader takes: no reader has ever been given file 32. A marker under plan 52 would call a non-eight mark the skill's fault only if it traced the reader to this sentence; H67's frozen line would count the mark itself.
passages.single_reading_wording: The eight marks (listed under "Stop" above, and in `references/reporting.md`) say what holds a part in place now

passages.quote: | where a job came from: given, fixed, added | provenance of a contract (declared, selected, constructed) | Part III | A question, and so each job in it, has a history as well as an answer. A job the tester wrote is declared by the tester. |
passages.reading_a: Line 113's ban is about parts, so a job has a provenance of its own and "fixed" is one of its words.
passages.reading_b: Line 113 says plainly "*borrowed* and *fixed* are not provenances", so this row and the report's "each tagged given, fixed or added" break the skill's own new rule, and the reader must drop the tag or stop calling it a provenance.
passages.resembles: H57's *fixed* stretch: "the mark stretched to cover the claimant's untested assertion, for which the skill has the provenance word *asserted*." H64 kind 1 counts two vocabularies; with this row and by-domain's design words the skill has four, and *fixed* sits in two of them - which is why the paragraph's opening census, "Two vocabularies, never mixed", can be read as a rule about two lists or as a statement that there are only two.
passages.would_break: Heading 2 requires "the jobs, each tagged given, fixed or added" while line 113 forbids *fixed* as a provenance; a reader following B leaves the tag off, and H67's own phase-2 amendment then marks the report PART ("a report with the seven headings but any of (a jobs list, a mark on every part, a change list) missing"). A marker under plan 52 would call the missing jobs list the reader's fault unless it traced the reader back to line 113, so the cost would be booked to the wrong layer.
passages.single_reading_wording: In line 113: "A part's provenance is one of fitted, built or asserted; a job's is one of given, fixed or added. Neither list's words go in the mark column: *asserted* is not a mark, and *borrowed* is not a part's provenance."

passages.quote: Its mark is *held*, by the condition that removing breaks it; it is never *fixed* for being derived.
passages.reading_a: Mark it held once you have found a condition whose removal breaks it, and name that condition: the proofs test has to be run first.
passages.reading_b: A derived conclusion is marked held because it is derived. The mark is settled by this passage, not by a test.
passages.resembles: H62's second new fault, the one this clause answers: "'The core derivation | Fixed / derived | It is an algebraic consequence of the definitions', P3 mode 2 repeat 1".
passages.would_break: A mark cell reading "held / derived - an algebraic consequence of the definitions", with no condition named: H62's row with one word changed, and now blessed by the skill. Where several conditions hold the conclusion only together, "the condition" in the singular also pulls against the joint-holding wording added to the same file. Under file 31, without the clause, the readers did the work anyway: H59 records "Five of the six named the conclusion as derived and dropped a condition in place of the flip", and the sixth "ran the flip and passed it". A marker under plan 52 would not call reading B the skill's fault, because the skill prescribes the mark; H67's frozen line looks only for *fixed* on a derived conclusion, which reading B avoids by writing *held*.
passages.single_reading_wording: Mark it *held* only when you can name a condition whose removal breaks it, and name that condition; where several conditions hold it only together, say so. Being derived is never a ground for *fixed*.

passages.quote: a test with no purchase on a document of this kind is said to have none, not left out
passages.reading_a: Where a test genuinely cannot bite on a document of this kind, write one line saying so - and still mark the part by whatever does hold it.
passages.reading_b: Any test you did not run may be written up as having no purchase, and that line stands in place of running it.
passages.resembles: File 54's largest gap, which change 2 answers by half: "The skill gives a reader with a single text nothing to do at this step and does not say that the right mark is *unknown*, with the test named." File 54's change 3, which would have named the mark, is not in file 32.
passages.would_break: A section 4 reading "Look inside: no purchase on a single document", with no part marked unknown and no test named - which satisfies H67's own prediction, "add a job and look inside both present (run, or said to have no purchase) in at least 40 of 48 FULL reports". It also feeds the marker's own edge-finding column: plan 52 defines CANNOT as "the reader says, or the document shows, that the test has no purchase on a document of this kind" and calls it "the mark that finds the skill's edges", and file 32 now teaches the reader that sentence, so a CANNOT under file 32 shows an instruction followed rather than an edge met. No report in the 195 ever said a test had no purchase (no CANNOT from either marker; my search found five "does not apply" hits, all the derived-conclusion flip redirect), so the reading cannot be checked against the record - the wording is new.
passages.single_reading_wording: a test that cannot bite on a document of this kind is named, with one line on why, and the part it would have settled is left *unknown* with that test named; it is never simply left out

passages.quote: Where a part came from (fitted, built, asserted) is a separate line, never a mark
passages.reading_a: A line of its own for each part, beside the mark - a second column in the part table.
passages.reading_b: One line for the whole explanation, which is where SKILL.md's report puts it: heading 4's "and where the parts came from".
passages.resembles: None recorded as a break. The nearest is H64 kind 1's diagnosis that the two lists are "two closed lists in the same style" - which reading A sets side by side in one table, and reading B keeps apart at the cost of any per-part provenance.
passages.would_break: Under reading A every mark has a provenance beside it and line 113's "Every part gets one of each" is checkable; under reading B the provenance is one sentence at the end and no part's provenance can be read off. Both are in the record: 36 of the 195 replies carry a "Provenance:" line, usually one sentence covering groups - "Provenance: P1-P6 are **built** ...; P7-P9 are **asserted**; P8 is **fitted**" (runs_repeat_31/F4-m2-r3), which gives one part two provenances and leaves two parts with none. A marker under plan 52 marks neither as a break: shape does not ask for provenance, so the field goes unmarked in either reading.
passages.single_reading_wording: Where a part came from (fitted, built, asserted) goes in its own column beside the mark, one for every part, and is never written as a mark

passages.quote: If the swap works as well, the part is loose.
passages.reading_a: Works = still does every job on the list, as the Remove bullet asks two lines above ("Does it still do every job?").
passages.reading_b: Works = reads or argues as plausibly.
passages.resembles: None recorded in 54, H57, H62 or H64. H64's trap line reaches it from outside ("The disagreements sit on four tests (poke, add a job, swap, inside), and those are where the skill's wording is loosest"; swap agreed 36 of 48). An outside reader in the Language project names the neighbouring hole in "near neighbour": "Sharing a dictionary neighbourhood is not a general guarantee of semantic equivalence. A change from one object kind to another can matter to response classes and must not be called harmless merely because it looks like a noun substitution."
passages.would_break: A *loose* mark earned by a sentence rather than by the jobs: "Swap the word: every real body 'must have extension in Length, Breadth, Thickness, and Mass' - and the sentence runs just as well" (runs_repeat_31/F4-m2-r3). Eleven of the 195 replies settle a swap with "works/reads/sounds just as well", and all but one or two name the job as well, so reading B is visible once or twice rather than often - this is the weakest-evidenced of my findings. A marker under plan 52 marks swap RAN either way ("applied with a concrete change or a named neighbour"), so it would not be called the skill's fault.
passages.single_reading_wording: If the swapped version still does every job on the list, the part is loose.

falsified.finding: by-domain.md's design words are a third mark vocabulary: "Every decision gets one of three honest marks: **held** ..., **free** ..., or **inherited**", so a reader meeting them writes "free" or "inherited" in the mark column, which is not one of the eight - and change 1's opening, "Two vocabularies, never mixed", tells the reader there are only two lists to keep apart.
falsified.why_dropped: The second reading was available to all 195 reports and nobody took it: my scan of every mark cell found no "free" and no "inherited" as a mark. Readers mapped it the way the skill's one line asks - H59 records "levers *loose*, 'a free design choice'" and "**Free and loose, and allowed to be:** the lilies of silver". The recorded break (file 54's break 2) runs the other way, free choice to *fixed*, and is covered by my *fixed* finding. The census reading of "Two vocabularies" survives only in the weaker form I kept, against the word list's job-provenance row.

falsified.finding: "it is never *fixed* for being derived" read as a blanket ban: a derived part could not be marked *fixed* even when the owner has put it outside the test and said so, which the eight marks reserve *fixed* for.
falsified.why_dropped: The modifier "for being derived" is in the sentence, so the rival reading does not fit as well; and the conflict case - a derived conclusion the owner also excluded - appears nowhere in the 195 reports. The nearest record instance runs the other way and is proper use: H59's four P3 runs marking substrate-independence *fixed* on "we shall here take it as a given", which H59's trap line says is not break 2. Kept only as a sentence inside the change-5 finding.

falsified.finding: The router row "judging something that matters | `references/the-idea-in-depth.md`, once per conversation" reads as a cap that licenses skipping the module on a second document in the same conversation, which plan 52 counts as a break ("a module the router failed to open when the case needed it").
falsified.why_dropped: No recorded reader skipped it: file 54 says the mode 2 reader "opened the idea-in-depth and reporting modules in every run without being told to", and the module lists in H57, H59 and H62 show "idea" opened in every one of the 24 mode 2 runs. The procedure's own line ("Read ... before a first full run in a conversation") settles the direction. Nothing in the record shows the harm.

falsified.finding: "**No scores.** Do not count confirmations, jobs or parts." reads as a ban on all counting, so a reader cannot write "two of the three parts are loose" and the report loses information it needs.
falsified.why_dropped: Reports count freely where counting is descriptive ("Exclusions plus weighting together, about 1.9 points", numbered parts P1-P11) and I found no report refusing a count it needed. The record's outside readers take the intended reading and say so in their own words ("No hardness score is assigned"). The ambiguity has no recorded cost.

falsified.finding: Change 4's "Writing the tag does not run the test" opens the mirror fault: a job proposed by the Add-a-job test is "a different act", so it takes no tag, and a part held only by it is marked plain *held* instead of *held if*.
falsified.why_dropped: Step 2 defines added as "you put it there", which plainly covers a job you propose in the test, so the rival reading does not fit as well - the skill's own swap test cuts it. No instance in the record: the reports tag reader-supplied jobs and use held if on them ("J5 ... *(added, by the narrator)*" with "P8 | Held if | only by J4", runs_repeat_31/F4-m2-r3). Dropped as speculation.

falsified.finding: "**Stop** when every part carries one of the eight marks" reads as a stopping rule rather than a closed list, so readers treat the mark column as free text - 169 distinct non-eight mark cells across the 195 replies.
falsified.why_dropped: Almost all 169 are one of the eight plus a qualifier ("held, renamed", "held by J5", "held, but its gauge is unstated"), which is compliance with detail, not a ninth mark. Only about a dozen sit outside the list, and those are the provenance words already carried by the two-vocabulary findings. The general claim does not survive its own count.

falsified.finding: "held, jointly with" is a ninth mark, so change 3 puts the skill in breach of its own "one of the eight marks" rule.
falsified.why_dropped: Under plan 52 a break has to be the skill's wording forcing a reader wrongly; here the skill instructs the phrase, so a reader writing it is obeying, and the marker rule that would flag it ("any word not one of the eight, as a mark") belongs to H67 phase 1, a plan H68 records as not run. Kept only as one sentence inside the joint-holding finding, where it bears on a marker's reading rather than a reader's.

what_this_does_not_show: Nothing here is a test result. (1) No reader has ever been given file 32. The 195 replies I searched ran under files 30 and 31, so for the five changed passages the record can show only what readers did with the wording those changes replaced; where I cite a count, it is against the unchanged words those readers actually read, and I say so in each finding. (2) I am the wrong kind of witness for my own headline claim: I read file 32 with the skill in hand and with H64's four kinds already in front of me, looking for second readings. A passage I can read two ways is not evidence that a reader will, and the two findings with no record support at all (change 1's pointer, the no-purchase clause) rest on my reading alone. (3) No count here is a rate. 96 of 103, 70 of 133, 12 mark cells, 3 provenance lines: these are counts of reports in one corpus from two models, mostly one run per box, and the record itself shows two runs of the same box disagreeing on the same sentence (file 54, the RFC 2001 gauge). My regular expressions decide what \"no reverse-test language\" means; a reader who ran reverse in words I did not search for is counted in the 96. (4) I tested no fix. Every \"fewest words\" wording is untested, written by the same hand that found the fault, and the skill's own rule applies to it: run it on the very thing it is meant to catch and on that thing's nearest innocent neighbour. None of that has been done. (5) Nothing here says file 32 is worse than file 31, or better. I did not compare them on any measure; H62's two faults under file 31 were one run each, and my findings are readings of wording, not counts of reports. (6) Severity is my judgement, not a mark from the record. For the two best-evidenced findings a marker under plan 52 in fact marked the tests RAN, so a marker could read this whole return as \"no break\" - which is itself the finding, and not something the marking can settle. (7) The supplied findings from Semantics and Language were pointers; I checked the three quotes I lean on (Language Lessons 35, Semantics S62's far-apart criterion, the Language audit's T42 note) verbatim in their files and did not check the rest. (8) I read only; I wrote nothing anywhere, and I did not open the Planning project or the 33 held-out sources.
